payload.author: hacs-bot
payload.body:
Thank you for submitting your repository to HACS (Home Assistant Community Store).

**Your submission is in the review queue:**
Your repository is waiting to be reviewed and included in HACS.

You can [view the current queue here](https://github.com/hacs/default/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+draft%3Afalse+sort%3Acreated-asc). Pull requests are processed in the order they were created, oldest first.

**What to avoid during review:**
To help reviewers work efficiently, don't do the following:

- **Comment on the pull request** - The reviewer will contact you when they have feedback or questions.
- **Open a new pull request** - This won't speed up the process and creates duplicate work.
- **Ask followers to comment on the pull request** - This won't speed up the process and may delay your review.
- **Merge in the default branch** - Only do this if a maintainer asks you to resolve a merge conflict.

**If you need to make changes:**
You can continue updating your repository while waiting for review. Changes to your repository will be reflected when the reviewer examines it. Only comment on the pull request if you need to withdraw your submission or have critical information for reviewers.

**About draft pull requests:**
Draft pull requests aren't included in the review queue. Your pull request may be marked as draft by a reviewer if issues need to be addressed. Once you've resolved all issues, mark it as ready for review to re-enter the queue.

**What happens next:**
Once a reviewer examines your submission, they'll either:

- Approve and merge your pull request if everything meets the requirements
- Request changes or ask questions if adjustments are needed

Thank you for submitting your repository to HACS (Home Assistant Community Store).

**Your submission is in the review queue:**
Your repository is waiting to be reviewed and included in HACS.

You can [view the current queue here](https://github.com/hacs/default/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+draft%3Afalse+sort%3Acreated-asc). Pull requests are processed in the order they were created, oldest first.

**What to avoid during review:**
To help reviewers work efficiently, don't do the following:

- **Comment on the pull request** - The reviewer will contact you when they have feedback or questions.
- **Open a new pull request** - This won't speed up the process and creates duplicate work.
- **Ask followers to comment on the pull request** - This won't speed up the process and may delay your review.
- **Merge in the default branch** - Only do this if a maintainer asks you to resolve a merge conflict.

**If you need to make changes:**
You can continue updating your repository while waiting for review. Changes to your repository will be reflected when the reviewer examines it. Only comment on the pull request if you need to withdraw your submission or have critical information for reviewers.

**About draft pull requests:**
Draft pull requests aren't included in the review queue. Your pull request may be marked as draft by a reviewer if issues need to be addressed. Once you've resolved all issues, mark it as ready for review to re-enter the queue.

**What happens next:**
Once a reviewer examines your submission, they'll either:

- Approve and merge your pull request if everything meets the requirements
- Request changes or ask questions if adjustments are needed

payload.author: lalexdotcom
payload.body:
In case #10238 is not the right way to do this and you would rather add the
`removed` entry yourselves, here it is ready to paste, so nobody has to rewrite it:

```json
  {
    "reason": "it is no longer maintained, and the same result can be had with the built-in Remote Calendar integration subscribed to the official Éducation nationale ICS feeds — one per zone, listed at https://data.education.gouv.fr/explore/assets/fr-en-calendrier-scolaire/ — plus a few template sensors",
    "removal_type": "remove",
    "repository": "lalexdotcom/ha-vacances-fr"
  },
```

`remove` rather than `blacklist`: nothing is wrong with the repository, I am
withdrawing it.

The `reason` is deliberately a lower-case clause with no trailing period, because
`async_handle_removed_repositories` interpolates it into the repair issue as
"Because {reason}, `{name}` has been removed from HACS." — so it has to read as
the middle of that sentence. The URL is fenced by spaces on both sides so an
autolinker cannot swallow the comma that follows it.

**Your submission is in the review queue:**
Your repository is waiting to be reviewed and included in HACS.

You can [view the current queue here](https://github.com/hacs/default/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+draft%3Afalse+sort%3Acreated-asc). Pull requests are processed in the order they were created, oldest first.

**What to avoid during review:**
To help reviewers work efficiently, don't do the following:

- **Comment on the pull request** - The reviewer will contact you when they have feedback or questions.
- **Open a new pull request** - This won't speed up the process and creates duplicate work.
- **Ask followers to comment on the pull request** - This won't speed up the process and may delay your review.
- **Merge in the default branch** - Only do this if a maintainer asks you to resolve a merge conflict.

**If you need to make changes:**
You can continue updating your repository while waiting for review. Changes to your repository will be reflected when the reviewer examines it. Only comment on the pull request if you need to withdraw your submission or have critical information for reviewers.

**About draft pull requests:**
Draft pull requests aren't included in the review queue. Your pull request may be marked as draft by a reviewer if issues need to be addressed. Once you've resolved all issues, mark it as ready for review to re-enter the queue.

**What happens next:**
Once a reviewer examines your submission, they'll either:

- Approve and merge your pull request if everything meets the requirements
- Request changes or ask questions if adjustments are needed

payload.author: luguina
payload.body:
The `Hassfest` check here is failing for a reason outside this PR, and I think it is currently
blocking every integration submission — #10116, #10115, #10114 and #10109 all fail the same check.

The job runs:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$integration":"/github/workspace/$domain" ghcr.io/home-assistant/hassfest:latest
```

home-assistant/core#178265 (merged 2026-08-10) narrowed the hassfest image's entrypoint so that
manifest discovery is limited to two locations relative to its `WORKDIR "/github/workspace"`:

```sh
manifests=$(
    { [ -d custom_components ] && find custom_components -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name "manifest.json"
      find . -maxdepth 1 -name "manifest.json"; } 2>/dev/null
)
```

Because the integration is mounted at `/github/workspace/$domain`, the manifest ends up at
`/github/workspace/kirri_beacon/manifest.json` — depth 2, but not under `custom_components/`. It
matches neither rule, so the entrypoint exits with `Error: No integrations found!` before hassfest
runs at all.

Mounting at `/github/workspace/custom_components/$domain` instead would satisfy the first rule.

For what it's worth, hassfest is green on the repository itself, because
`home-assistant/actions/hassfest@master` mounts the whole checkout and so
`custom_components/kirri_beacon/manifest.json` matches:
https://github.com/luguina/kirri-beacon-hass/actions/runs/32139392472/job/95718185952

Happy to rebase or re-run once the workflow is sorted — no rush from my side.

payload.body:
Thank you for submitting your repository to HACS (Home Assistant Community Store).

**Your submission is in the review queue:**
Your repository is waiting to be reviewed and included in HACS.

You can [view the current queue here](https://github.com/hacs/default/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+draft%3Afalse+sort%3Acreated-asc). Pull requests are processed in the order they were created, oldest first.

**What to avoid during review:**
To help reviewers work efficiently, don't do the following:

- **Comment on the pull request** - The reviewer will contact you when they have feedback or questions.
- **Open a new pull request** - This won't speed up the process and creates duplicate work.
- **Ask followers to comment on the pull request** - This won't speed up the process and may delay your review.
- **Merge in the default branch** - Only do this if a maintainer asks you to resolve a merge conflict.

**If you need to make changes:**
You can continue updating your repository while waiting for review. Changes to your repository will be reflected when the reviewer examines it. Only comment on the pull request if you need to withdraw your submission or have critical information for reviewers.

**About draft pull requests:**
Draft pull requests aren't included in the review queue. Your pull request may be marked as draft by a reviewer if issues need to be addressed. Once you've resolved all issues, mark it as ready for review to re-enter the queue.

**What happens next:**
Once a reviewer examines your submission, they'll either:

- Approve and merge your pull request if everything meets the requirements
- Request changes or ask questions if adjustments are needed

payload.author: Jos1958
payload.body:
hassfest in HACS/default cannot find my integration
Please note that the hassfest runs fine in my own repository: https://github.com/Jos1958/ha-helios-calculator
Others have reported the same problem (see the issue below in the hacs/integration issues).

I fixed the folder structure by adding a dummy file under the custom_components hoping this may help.
The validation jobs (including hassfest) are not running automatically again!
The jobs was run only once after I submitted the pull request.
I do not have the authorization to restart the jobs in hacs/default.

Can you please start a re-run of the validation jobs to check that this fixes the problem.

payload.author: Jos1958
payload.body:
I investigated the Hassfest failure further. The integration repository itself passes Hassfest successfully. I also found a way to re-run the Hassfest by committing my hacs/default changes again.

The HACS validation workflow finds manifest.json using integration_path.py, but then mounts only custom_components/helios_calculator as /github/workspace/helios_calculator before running ghcr.io/home-assistant/hassfest:latest.

This results in Error: No integrations found!.

The same repository passes Hassfest when the normal custom_components/helios_calculator structure is provided to Hassfest.

As mentioned in https://github.com/hacs/integration/issues/5483 there are many (or may be even all) new integrations that fail. Can this be related to a recent change in Hassfest's integration discovery?

payload.author: eman
payload.body:
The HACS action and all repository checks pass. The hassfest failure is an upstream workflow regression: the latest hassfest image now discovers custom integrations only at the workspace root or `custom_components/<domain>`, while this repository mounts submissions at `/github/workspace/<domain>`, causing `Error: No integrations found!` before TariffKit is validated. The same regression affects other current submissions, including #10018.

I reproduced the failure locally and confirmed TariffKit passes every hassfest validator when mounted at the documented location. The one-line workflow correction is in #10020.

The hacs/default checks workflow has a dedicated renamed-repositories run type selected by the renamed-repositories label. All current checks are green and maintainer_can_modify is enabled. This PR likely needs that maintainer label so the rename path can be accepted.

Hi, just a note regarding the Hassfest failure.

The integration structure has been checked and follows the standard Home Assistant layout:

custom_components/knvb_rinus/manifest.json

The integration is present on the default branch and the manifest.json is valid. The current Hassfest check fails with:

It appears that the current HACS/Hassfest validation is not detecting the standalone integration when it is mounted by the HACS check.

The integration itself passes Hassfest validation when run against the integration directory directly.

Just mentioning this so the No integrations found error isn't mistaken for a missing or incorrectly placed integration.

payload.title: Update NeverDry in integration catalog: drake69/NeverDry -> never-dry/NeverDry

payload.author: hacs-bot
payload.body: **Your branch seems out of date.** Please update your branch with the latest changes from the base branch.

payload.author: drake69
payload.body:
The automated message above looks like a false positive, and I don't think I can clear it from my side, so I'm noting the details here for whoever picks this up.

This is a rename, not an addition: `drake69/NeverDry` -> `never-dry/NeverDry`, same repository and same GitHub id (`1204571373`), only the owner changed. NeverDry is already in the default list, added in #6911. I moved it to an organization so that contributors can hold the `triage` role, which personal repositories do not offer.

A rename diff necessarily removes one entry and adds another, so `getFileDiff` returns two elements and the PR lands in the `changedRepos.length > 1` branch; since `additions` is 1, it selects the "branch seems out of date" wording rather than the "single repository change" one. The branch itself is current: it is based on master HEAD (`d97dc850`), `behind_by` is 0, and the merge base of the comparison is master HEAD itself.

The diff has the same shape as the maintainer-opened rename PRs (#9319, #9320, #9321): +1/-1 on a single catalog file, with the entry moved to its new alphabetical position between `neuhausf/...` and `nexhome-org/...`. The remaining checks are green, including `Sorted` and `Editable PR`.

If rename PRs from contributors aren't wanted and this is better handled by the existing rename tooling, I'm happy to close it - no objection either way.

payload.author: drake69
payload.body:
Closing this: per https://hacs.xyz/docs/publish/update/ a PR is not needed for a rename or transfer, the HACS team updates the records automatically. Apologies for the noise - I'd missed that page.

The transfer for reference: `drake69/NeverDry` -> `never-dry/NeverDry`, same id `1204571373`.

Thank you for submitting your repository to HACS (Home Assistant Community Store).

**Your submission is in the review queue:**
Your repository is waiting to be reviewed and included in HACS.

You can [view the current queue here](https://github.com/hacs/default/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+draft%3Afalse+sort%3Acreated-asc). Pull requests are processed in the order they were created, oldest first.

**What to avoid during review:**
To help reviewers work efficiently, don't do the following:

- **Comment on the pull request** - The reviewer will contact you when they have feedback or questions.
- **Open a new pull request** - This won't speed up the process and creates duplicate work.
- **Ask followers to comment on the pull request** - This won't speed up the process and may delay your review.
- **Merge in the default branch** - Only do this if a maintainer asks you to resolve a merge conflict.

**If you need to make changes:**
You can continue updating your repository while waiting for review. Changes to your repository will be reflected when the reviewer examines it. Only comment on the pull request if you need to withdraw your submission or have critical information for reviewers.

**About draft pull requests:**
Draft pull requests aren't included in the review queue. Your pull request may be marked as draft by a reviewer if issues need to be addressed. Once you've resolved all issues, mark it as ready for review to re-enter the queue.

**What happens next:**
Once a reviewer examines your submission, they'll either:

- Approve and merge your pull request if everything meets the requirements
- Request changes or ask questions if adjustments are needed

payload.body: > Hi @DTekNOdev, thanks for the submission! 👋 > > One issue to fix before this can be added: the card renders alert fields that come from external feeds (USGS/NWS/RSS, per the README) directly into the DOM without escaping. In `_renderAlert` (and `_renderDismissedAlert`), the values `${alert.title}`, `${alert.message}`, `${alert.area}`, and `${alert.instruction}` are interpolated straight into `this.shadowRoot.innerHTML`. Because that text comes from third-party feeds, a feed item whose title or message contains markup like `` would execute script in the Home Assistant frontend. > > Please escape those feed-derived values before inserting them (for example, render them via `textContent`, or run them through an HTML-escape helper) so untrusted feed content can't inject markup. Once that's in place, cut a new release and re-request review. > > ../Frenck Done and released. There were additional places that needed similar treatment, all fixed. Tested that the content is still shown the same using alerting integration "norway_alerts" in test mode, and the feed derived content examples for NWS etc as demonstrated in the README.

payload.author: frenck
payload.body:
Hi @ZaneThePython, thanks for the submission! 👋 A few things to address before this can be added: 1. Command scope: in `coordinator.py`, commands pushed from the OpenJibo server are turned into house-wide `light` and `climate` service calls (`_handle_command`, `_handle_lights_named` around line 285, `_set_climate_temperature` around line 730). The named-light and climate handlers aren't scoped to the Jibo's own area, and individual command frames carry no per-message authentication (trust is established once at pairing). That means whoever operates or can impersonate that server can toggle any light and set any thermostat in the home. Please scope actuation to the device's configured area (and/or add per-command authentication) so a compromised or spoofed server can't drive the whole house. 2. `manifest.json` `version` is `0.2.0.0` while the release tag is `v1.0.3.4`; please keep them in sync. 3. `manifest.json` `issue_tracker` points to `https://github.com/ZaneThePython/openjibo-hacs/issues`, a different repository than the one being submitted (`Jibo-Revival-Group/openjibo-haint`). Please point it at this repo's issues. Once those are addressed, cut a new release and re-request review. ../Frenck

                       

Blogging my personal ramblings at frenck.dev

payload.author: fschubi
payload.body:
Hi @frenck, thanks for the careful review — you were right, that was a real hole. Fixed in [v2.4.2](https://github.com/fschubi/shutter_pilot/releases/tag/v2.4.2).

**Write commands are admin-gated.** All mutating WebSocket commands now carry `@websocket_api.require_admin` (outermost, as in HA core):

- `shutter_pilot/save_area`, `shutter_pilot/delete_area`
- `shutter_pilot/save_shutter`, `shutter_pilot/delete_shutter`
- `shutter_pilot/save_settings` — not in your list, but it writes to the config entry options too (weather entity, drive verification), so I gated it as well
- `shutter_pilot/set_master_enabled`, `shutter_pilot/set_auto_mode`

`shutter_pilot/get_status` is read-only and stays as it is.

**One deliberate deviation, and I want to be upfront about it:** I kept `require_admin=False` on the panel registration. The panel is not only the config UI — it is also the control surface for the shutters (up / stop / down / sun protection / ventilate). Those buttons call the regular `cover.*` services, which Home Assistant authorizes on its own, and non-admin household members legitimately use them to operate their own shutters. Hiding the panel would take that away from them.

Instead the panel adapts to the user's permissions via `hass.user.is_admin`: without admin rights it renders only the dashboard with the control buttons — no tabs for areas, shutters or settings, no master switch, per-area auto switch disabled, and a note explaining why. That part is convenience only; the actual boundary is server-side, so a hand-crafted WebSocket message from a non-admin gets `Unauthorized` regardless of what the frontend shows.

If you'd still prefer the panel itself to be admin-only, say the word and I'll flip it — I just didn't want to silently remove the shutter controls from non-admin users without flagging the trade-off.

Ready for another look.

payload.author: frenck
payload.body: Hi @peternijssen, thanks for the submission! 👋 The rebase is sorted, so here is the proper review pass. I looked at 2.7.5 rather than the 2.7.2 that `releases/latest` pointed at when you opened this, which is worth bearing in mind for the PR body. One blocker. **`hacs.json` declares `"homeassistant": "2024.7.0"`, and the integration needs 2024.12.0.** Three separate things put the bar above what you have declared: - `coordinator.py:60` and `:385` pass `config_entry=entry` to `DataUpdateCoordinator.__init__`. That keyword has zero occurrences in core's `update_coordinator.py` at 2024.10.0 and one at 2024.11.0, so on 2024.7 through 2024.10 setup dies with a `TypeError` before the first poll. - `config_flow.py:163` and `:165` call `_abort_if_unique_id_mismatch` and `_get_reauth_entry`, both absent from `config_entries.py` at 2024.10.0 and present at 2024.11.0. - `DhlOptionsFlowHandler` subclasses a plain `OptionsFlow` and reads `self.config_entry` at `:197` and `:208` without ever assigning it, which your own docstring at `:185-186` says is deliberate. That property is on `OptionsFlowWithConfigEntry` at 2024.11.0 and only moves onto the base `OptionsFlow` at 2024.12.0, so on 2024.11 the integration sets up fine and then raises `AttributeError` the moment someone opens the options dialog. 2024.12.0 is the exact floor. `README.md:41` needs the same bump. Worth noting that green HACS and hassfest do not catch this: the action checks that the key parses, not that the value is true. Two documentation things worth folding into the same round, since you will be in the README anyway: - **`README.md:157` says the `returning` status is "not yet observed; will be added once the raw indicator is confirmed".** `parcels.py` maps 46 raw DHL statuses to `ParcelStatus.RETURNING`, and your own 2.7.2 release notes announce exactly that. Anyone writing an automation on `returning` reads that row and concludes it will never fire. - **Three shipped entities are undocumented.** The sensor list at `README.md:104-120` covers eight sensors and never mentions the `last_update` diagnostic sensor (`sensor.py:585-614`), the `deliveries` calendar (`calendar.py:51-126`) or the `refresh` button (`button.py:27-50`). The calendar in particular is a whole entity people are getting without being told. One question rather than a request. `parcels.py:501` returns `parcels[:filter_amount]` under a comment saying "return the most recent N", but it is called at `coordinator.py:146` on the raw API list and the sort by `delivered_at` only happens afterwards at `:159-163`. If DHL's `receiver-parcel-api/parcels` endpoint does not return newest first, users picking "number of parcels" get an arbitrary N rather than the most recent N. I could not verify the endpoint's ordering, so I am asking rather than asserting. The `days` branch at `:493-498` is unaffected. Smaller notes you can take or leave: `custom_components/dhl_nl/brand/icon.png` is about 9 KB that nothing reads, since core only serves in-tree brand assets from 2026.3.0; `parcels.py:404` and `:449` both exclude a parcel whose payload is missing `isReturn`, so a field DHL stopped sending would silently empty every sensor rather than fail loudly; `ARCHITECTURE.md:9-21` lists nine component files against fifteen shipped and names a `DhlPackagesSensor` that no longer exists. The rest is in good shape. The reauth path is wired correctly and does not fall back into `async_step_user`, the coordinator raises rather than replaying cached data on failure, the per-entry cookie jar with `connector_owner=False` is exactly right for multiple accounts, `_unrecorded_attributes` is set on every large-attribute sensor, `requirements` is empty, and the en and nl translations are at full key parity. ../Frenck

payload.body: Hi @tajniak81, thanks for the submission! 👋 Reviewing v3.3.1. Two things need fixing. **1. The declared floor is one release too low, and "Add notification target" fails on it.** `hacs.json` says `2025.3.0`, but the subentry flow calls `self._get_entry()` at `config_flow.py:468` (inside `_gateway_devices`) and again at `:415`. `ConfigSubentryFlow` has no `_get_entry` method before 2025.4.0: I counted `def _get_entry` in core's `config_entries.py` and it is 0 at 2025.3.0 and 0 at 2025.3.4, then 1 at 2025.4.0, at line 3464 inside `class ConfigSubentryFlow` which opens at 3391. It is not inherited either. This is on the add path, not just the edit path: `async_step_user` goes straight to `async_step_sim` at `:388`, whose schema builds the SIM options through `_gateway_devices`. So on any 2025.3.x install the very first "Add notification target" raises `AttributeError` at step two of two. Neither HACS validation nor hassfest catches it, because neither imports the module against a pinned core version. Everything else in the integration is satisfied at 2025.3.0, so `2025.4.0` is the exact right floor. README:42 needs the same bump. **2. The per-phone sensors report "connected" straight through a gateway outage.** `coordinator.py:66` returns `GsmNodeData(healthy=False, devices=previous.devices)` and `:76` returns `GsmNodeData(healthy=True, devices=previous.devices)`, in both cases replaying the last known device list without raising, so `last_update_success` stays true. `GsmNodePhoneSensor.available` at `binary_sensor.py:110-112` is `super().available and self._device is not None`, and the device is still in the replayed list, so `is_on` at `:115-118` keeps returning the cached `status == "online"`. Your docstring at `coordinator.py:57-61` and README:343-345 both argue this case, and for the **gateway** sensor the reasoning is right: an unreachable API Server should read as `off`, not unavailable, because that is precisely the state the entity exists to report. But the phone sensors are a different question. When the gateway is unreachable, a phone's connectivity is unknown, not unchanged, and a dashboard showing green phones behind a red gateway is telling the user something false. It also defeats the automation shape README:201-203 recommends. Dropping `devices` on the unhealthy path, or gating `GsmNodePhoneSensor.available` on `coordinator.data.healthy`, fixes it without touching the gateway sensor. Three smaller things: - **README:434-436 contradicts the code and the rest of the README.** It says "Only plain SMS and calls are wired up... The API Server also accepts MMS... those have no service here yet", but MMS is fully wired: `services.py:118-121` validates it, `client.py:168-172` sends subject and attachments, and `notify.py:75-76` sets `NotifyEntityFeature.TITLE` for MMS targets. README:118-126 documents it working. Stale paragraph from before 3.3.0. - **`icons.json` is missing `send`,** your headline action per README:22. It lists only `send_sms` and `call`, so `gsmnode.send` draws the generic icon in the action picker. - **`NOTICE` in the shipped v3.3.1 still reads "Copyright 2026 FreeFallDev".** I can see the rebrand commit landed a day after the tag, so this clears itself on the next release. `custom_components/gsmnode/brand/` is 40 KB that nothing reads below 2026.3.0, but your README already says so explicitly, so I will leave that as your call rather than a finding. The rest is genuinely good work: HMAC-signed webhooks with a replay window, a real reauth flow, unique IDs throughout, empty `requirements`, no Lovelace tampering, byte-identical `strings.json` and `translations/en.json`, and a panel that unregisters itself cleanly on unload. ../Frenck

payload.body:
Hi @pickerin, thanks for the submission! 👋

I reviewed v1.1.9 rather than the v1.1.7 the PR body links, so please refresh those links. Two things need fixing before this can go in.

**1. The reauth flow can never complete.** `config_flow.py:73-75` is:

```python
async def async_step_reauth(self, entry_data: dict) -> FlowResult:
    """Handle reauth when credentials expire."""
    return await self.async_step_user()
```

and `async_step_user` unconditionally runs `await self.async_set_unique_id(email.lower())` followed by `self._abort_if_unique_id_configured()` at `:33-34`. During reauth the existing entry already carries that unique ID, and `_abort_if_unique_id_configured` has no reauth exemption in core: its only early return is the `SOURCE_IGNORE` plus `SOURCE_USER` case, and everything else raises `AbortFlow("already_configured")`. So the form renders, the user types the new password, and the flow aborts. Even with that removed, `:48` calls `async_create_entry`, which core rejects inside a reauth flow with "Creates a new entry in a 'reauth' flow, when it is expected to update an existing entry and abort".

This is reachable in normal use: `coordinator.py:39` and `:101` both raise `ConfigEntryAuthFailed`, which is exactly what starts a reauth flow, and Whirlpool password grants do expire. Right now the only recovery is deleting and re-adding the integration, which loses every entity ID and all history. The fix is a reauth confirm step that skips the unique-ID abort and ends with `async_update_reload_and_abort(self._get_reauth_entry(), data_updates=...)`.

**2. An appliance that goes offline keeps reporting as running, forever.** `api.py:508-532`, `get_state` publishes `getState`, sleeps two seconds, and then returns `self._device_state.get(said)` with no check that a response actually arrived. `_on_mqtt_message` stores state without a timestamp, so there is nothing to compare against, and `:513-514` returns the same cached dict when there is no MQTT connection at all. The coordinator then sets `"online": state is not None` at `coordinator.py:93`, so once a device has ever reported, `state` is never `None` again: `online` stays true, `sensor.py:411-417` keeps the entity available, and `_async_update_data` returns normally so `last_update_success` stays true. An unplugged washer shows `running` with 42 minutes remaining indefinitely, and nothing appears in the log.

You clearly intended to handle this. `const.py:13` is `STALE_TIMEOUT = 300  # 5 minutes, mark unavailable after this`, and that constant is referenced nowhere else in the repository. Timestamp the writes in `_on_mqtt_message` and have `get_state` return `None` once the newest state is older than that.

Smaller things:

- **`awsiotsdk>=1.0.0` and `boto3>=1.20.0`** are both open-ended. A future major breaks users silently; please pin them.
- **The entire sensor platform sits inside a bare `except ImportError: pass`.** `sensor.py:187` opens a `try` around the Home Assistant imports and everything down to `:442`, closed by `:443-444`. If any of those names ever moves, the module defines no `async_setup_entry`, the integration loads with zero entities, and nothing is logged. That is a test-convenience hack that has shipped into production code.
- **`strings.json` is in the wrong place.** It sits at `translations/strings.json`; Home Assistant expects it at the component root. The content is byte-identical to `translations/en.json`, so nothing is missing today.
- **`brand/` is dead weight at the declared floor.** `hacs.json` says `2025.7.2`, and core only serves in-tree brand assets from 2026.3.0, so the v1.1.7 release note claiming the icon "now shows in the HA frontend" is not true for anyone on your stated minimum. Either raise the floor or submit the assets to [home-assistant/brands](https://github.com/home-assistant/brands).
- **README:5** still carries a `1.1.0` version badge, and the Installation section documents the custom-repository flow, which will be wrong onc

payload.body: Hi @pickerin, thanks for the submission! 👋 Reviewing v0.6.8. Two things need fixing. **1. The declared `homeassistant` floor is too low by three releases.** `hacs.json` says `2024.11.0`, but `config_flow.py:13` imports `ZeroconfServiceInfo` from `homeassistant.helpers.service_info.zeroconf`. That module does not exist in core before 2025.2.0: it is a 404 at both 2024.12.0 and 2025.1.0, and a 200 at 2025.2.0. Since `config_flow: true`, anyone HACS offers this to between 2024.11 and 2025.1 gets an `ImportError` and cannot set it up at all. The same release is the independent floor for the card registration below: at 2024.11.0 `hass.data["lovelace"]` is still a plain dict, so `getattr(lovelace, "resources", None)` at `__init__.py:127` returns `None` and the function quietly returns at `:129`, which would make README:86 ("The card registers itself as a Lovelace resource automatically") untrue on every version in the gap. One bump to `2025.2.0` covers both. **2. Drop the Lovelace resource registration entirely.** `__init__.py:138` calls `resources.async_create_item({"res_type": "module", "url": card_url})` and `:142` calls `async_update_item`. There is no `async_delete_item` anywhere in the repository and no `async_remove_entry` at all; `async_unload_entry` at `:256-257` only unloads the platforms. Once the user removes the integration, `/busybar-static/busybar-card.js?v=0.6.8` stays in `.storage/lovelace_resources` while the static path registered at `:155-163` is gone, so every dashboard render fetches a dead module with nothing to point the user at the cause. Integrations should not write into a user's Lovelace configuration. Please document the resource for users to add themselves, or register the JS through `add_extra_js_url`, which is per-run and cleans itself up. Smaller things: - **The five services registered at `__init__.py:237-251` are never removed.** There is no `async_remove` call anywhere, so after the last entry is deleted the handlers survive and raise `BusyBarError("No BUSY Bar configured")` from `:104`. - **The API key travels in the WebSocket URL query string** (`api.py:44`, `?x-api-token=...`), and `ws.py:67` logs connection errors whose text includes the request URL. Debug level only, but that puts the credential in the log. - **`custom_components/busybar/brand/`** ships 45 KB that nothing reads. Core only serves in-tree brand assets from 2026.3.0, well above your floor even after the bump. Submit them to [home-assistant/brands](https://github.com/home-assistant/brands) instead. - **`www/busybar-card.js:448`** still prints `0.6.7` in the console banner of a 0.6.8 release. Also worth knowing: no checks have run on the current head of this PR, so please rebase on master alongside the fixes. The rest reads well. The reauth flow is properly wired, the coordinator raises rather than replaying stale data, `strings.json` and `translations/en.json` are byte-identical, and the entity and service accounting matches the README exactly. ../Frenck

payload.body:
Hi @lucasgiovanny, thanks for the submission! 👋 I reviewed v0.53.0 rather than the v0.20.1 the PR body links, so please refresh those links too. This is a strong submission and most of it is in good shape. One thing needs to change before it can go in. **Drop the Lovelace resource registration entirely.** `__init__.py:215-228` reaches into `hass.data.get("lovelace")`, then calls `resources.async_update_item` at `:226` and `resources.async_create_item` at `:228` for both `card.js` and `scene-card.js`. There is no `async_delete_item` anywhere in the repository, and neither `async_unload_entry` (`:431-442`) nor `async_remove_entry` (`:445-449`) touches the resource collection. So when a user removes the integration and uninstalls it, the static paths registered at `:165-171` disappear with the files while the two resource entries stay in `.storage/lovelace_resources`, and every dashboard load fetches two 404s forever with nothing in the UI to explain why. Integrations should not be writing into a user's Lovelace configuration at all. You already have the right mechanism sitting next to it: `add_extra_js_url` at `:192-195`. Please use that path unconditionally and remove the resource-collection branch. Two smaller things: - **A non-ASCII token in the URL path returns a 500 with a traceback, not a 404.** `http.py:157` calls `hmac.compare_digest(known_token, token)`, which refuses non-ASCII `str` and raises `TypeError: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported`. `_entry_for_token` runs before the invalid-token rate limiter in `_check_token`, so a request to something like `/api/pool_maintenance_tracker/café/page` on an instance with at least one pool set up is neither rate-limited nor counted, and just logs a traceback. An `isascii()` guard fixes it. - **`segno>=1.6.1`** has no upper bound, so a future major with a changed API gets pulled in silently. For what it is worth, the parts of this that usually go wrong are right: the declared floor of `2024.12.0` is exactly the one the code requires, the unauthenticated views are deliberately designed and honestly documented, the translations are complete across all seven languages, and the entity accounting is exact. ../Frenck

                       

Blogging my personal ramblings at frenck.dev

frenck
payload.body: Hi @Migux13, thanks for the submission! 👋 Two housekeeping items first: this branch conflicts with master again (master has moved into the same part of the `integration` file since your last rebase), and no checks have run on the current head. Please rebase on the latest master so the validation actually runs. On the integration itself, reviewing release 1.3.0: **1. `hacs.json` has no `homeassistant` key at all, and the real floor is 2024.12.0.** `ZaragozaTransporteOptionsFlow.async_step_init` reads `self.config_entry` at `config_flow.py:194` without ever setting it, which relies on the base `OptionsFlow.config_entry` property. That property does not exist in core before 2024.12.0, so on anything older the options flow raises `AttributeError`. Please add `"homeassistant": "2024.12.0"`. **2. The tram sensors have no unique ID.** `ZaragozaTramSensor.__init__` sets `entity_id` but never `_attr_unique_id`, so the two tram entities per stop never land in the entity registry. Users cannot rename them, cannot assign them to an area, and cannot hide or disable them. The bus sensors do this correctly at `sensor.py:181` and `:185`; the tram ones need the same treatment. **3. Three hardcoded `self.entity_id` assignments** (`sensor.py:122`, `:182`, `:186`). Let Home Assistant derive the entity ID from the name and unique ID. Setting it by hand bypasses the registry's collision handling and silently breaks when a user renames the entity. **4. There is no `available` property and no failure signalling.** When the API call fails or returns a non-200, the sensors write Spanish sentences into the state: `"Error al conectar"`, `"Sin datos"`, `"Parada no encontrada"` (`sensor.py:139-152`). A sensor whose state is otherwise a number of minutes should go unavailable on a failed update, not report prose. As it stands, any automation comparing the state to a number breaks, and history is polluted with string states. **5. `requests.get(API_URL)` at `sensor.py:133` has no timeout.** The two bus helpers pass `timeout=15`; the tram one does not. An unresponsive endpoint will hold an executor thread indefinitely. **6. `requirements: ["requests"]` is completely unpinned.** Please pin it to a version range you have tested against. **7. `translations/en.json` is byte-identical to `translations/es.json`,** and both are Spanish. English users get a Spanish config flow. Either translate it properly or drop the file so it is at least obvious that only Spanish is provided. Once those are addressed, cut a new release and rebase the branch so the checks can run. ../Frenck

payload.author: frenck
payload.body:
Hi @fapgomes, thanks for the submission! 👋 The way this integration drives Bluetooth needs rework before it can be added, because it interferes with Home Assistant's own Bluetooth stack: 1. `device.py` monkeypatches pygatt at import and resets the shared host adapter: it runs `hciconfig hci0 reset` and calls `adapter.start(reset_on_start=True)`, and spawns `bluetoothctl` scan/connect/disconnect subprocesses. Home Assistant owns and manages the Bluetooth adapter, so resetting `hci0` mid-operation can knock every other BLE integration offline. Please use Home Assistant's Bluetooth APIs (bleak via the `bluetooth`/`bleak-retry-connector` stack, which you already depend on) instead of resetting the adapter or shelling out to `bluetoothctl`/`hciconfig`. 2. The code imports `lywsd02` (bluepy-based) as its "canonical" path, but neither `lywsd02` nor `bluepy` is declared in the manifest `requirements`, so that path is never actually available to users. Either drop it or declare the real dependencies. 3. The `mac` parameter of the time-setting service isn't validated before it's placed into a `bluetoothctl` stdin script (the config-flow path is validated, but the service path isn't). Please validate it as a MAC address. Once the Bluetooth handling goes through Home Assistant's APIs, cut a new release and re-request review. ../Frenck

                       

Blogging my personal ramblings at frenck.dev

payload.author: frenck
payload.body:
Hi @fapgomes, thanks for coming back to this! 👋 I checked v0.16.0 against my earlier review and all three points are properly addressed: the pygatt monkeypatch, the `hciconfig hci0 reset` and the `bluetoothctl` subprocesses are gone in favour of bleak through Home Assistant's stack with `bleak-retry-connector`; the undeclared `lywsd02`/`bluepy` path is gone; and the service `mac` argument now goes through `is_valid_mac` before it is used. Nicely done, that is exactly what I was asking for. One blocker is left, and it is not one I raised last time. **`hacs.json` declares `homeassistant: "2024.1.0"`, but the integration cannot load there.** `config_flow.py:15` imports `ConfigFlowResult` from `homeassistant.config_entries`. That name does not exist in core until 2024.4.0 (it is defined at `config_entries.py:259` in the 2024.4.0 tag, and there are no occurrences of it at 2024.3.0). Anyone on 2024.1 through 2024.3 who installs this gets an `ImportError` the moment the config flow is loaded. Please raise the floor to `2024.4.0`. Two smaller things while you are in there: - `bleak-retry-connector>=3.0` has no upper bound, so a future 4.0 with a changed API gets pulled in silently. Worth capping. - `custom_components/lywsd02_clock/brand/` ships about 260 KB that nothing reads: Home Assistant only serves in-tree brand assets from 2026.3.0 onwards, far above your floor. If you want the icons to show up, submit them to [home-assistant/brands](https://github.com/home-assistant/brands) instead. Also, the PR body still links v0.14.2 as the current release. Please point it at whatever you cut next. ../Frenck

payload.author: fapgomes
payload.body:
Hi @frenck, thanks for the detailed review — all three points have been addressed and the Bluetooth handling has been fully rewritten (released as v0.15.0; current release is v0.16.0).

**1. Bluetooth handling** — `device.py` now uses Home Assistant's Bluetooth APIs exclusively: `bluetooth.async_ble_device_from_address` / `async_register_callback` for discovery, and `bleak-retry-connector`'s `establish_connection` for connections. The pygatt/gatttool path (including the `hciconfig` adapter reset and the monkeypatch), all `bluetoothctl` subprocesses, and the raw bluezdbus backend usage are gone — no subprocesses and no adapter manipulation remain anywhere in the integration. It also works through ESPHome Bluetooth proxies now.

While rewriting I found why that fallback ladder existed in the first place: the old HA-API path had never actually worked — it looked devices up with a lowercase MAC (which never matches the Bluetooth manager's cache) and called `connect()` on the already-connected client returned by `establish_connection`. With those fixed, the HA stack path works reliably. One device quirk surfaced during live verification: the LYWSD02 sometimes drops the link right after connecting while still applying the write, so the write phase does bounded retries on a fresh connection and verifies lost acknowledgements by reading the time back — all through HA's APIs.

**2. Dependencies** — the never-installed `lywsd02`/`bluepy` path was removed entirely; `requirements` is now just `bleak-retry-connector>=3.0` (imported directly), alongside the existing `bluetooth_adapters` dependency.

**3. Service `mac` validation** — the `set_time` service schema now validates `mac` as a MAC address, and `timestamp`/`tz_offset` are range-validated as well.

Also added since the review: a test suite (34 tests) running in CI alongside the hassfest/HACS actions, and a battery diagnostic sensor.

Verified end-to-end on real hardware (HAOS 2026.7.4, both local adapter and ESPHome proxy). Re-requesting review as asked — thanks again!

payload.author: frenck
payload.body: Hi @amery74, thanks for the submission! 👋 I reviewed v1.3.0 (the PR body still links v1.2.3, so please update that too). A few things need fixing before this can go in. **1. `set_maintenance_mode` raises `NameError` on every call.** `__init__.py:199` calls `_coordinator_for_call(hass, call)`, and that name is not defined anywhere in the package. Every other handler in the same file uses `await _coordinator()`. As shipped, `pool_pilot.set_maintenance_mode` fails 100% of the time. **2. `manifest.json` version is `1.3.0-beta` on a non-prerelease tag.** The tag is `v1.3.0`; the manifest should match. **3. There is no `translations/en.json`.** Only `fr.json` ships. Home Assistant loads translations from `/translations/.json`, and `strings.json` is not read at runtime for custom integrations, so on any English install nothing loads for `pool_pilot`: the whole config flow and every entity name renders as a raw key. French users get the strings; nobody else does. **4. Two documented service fields are rejected by the schema.** `services.yaml:316` and `:325` offer `free_chlorine_slow` and `total_chlorine_slow` as fields of `update_strip_test`, but `UPDATE_STRIP_TEST_SCHEMA` at `__init__.py:80-89` is a plain `vol.Schema` with no `extra=vol.ALLOW_EXTRA`, unlike the five other schemas in that file which all have it. Filling either field in the UI fails validation with "extra keys not allowed". Either add the two keys to the schema or drop them from `services.yaml`. **5. `codeowners` points at an account that does not exist.** The manifest lists `@antonin-mery`; there is no such GitHub user. payload.body:
Hi @Pablo1732, thanks for the rebase. The conflict is cleared and all twelve checks are green on the head, so here is the proper pass.

Reviewed against `v1.1.0`, which is what the PR body links. Six sensor types documented and six shipped, matching names in `strings.json`, `en.json` and `de.json`, no orphans in either direction. Every claim in the v1.1.0 notes traced to code, including the migration path: I fetched the archived `ms32035/home-assistant-ubibot` and its unique ID format is byte-identical to yours, so the history-preservation claim genuinely holds. Taking over an abandoned integration with a working import flow, a device-identifier rewrite and a credit line in the README is the right way to do this.

## The declared floor is three releases too low, and it is a hard failure

`hacs.json` line 4 declares `"homeassistant": "2024.8.0"`, and README lines 38 and 190 repeat it.

`__init__.py` line 64 passes `config_entry=entry` to `DataUpdateCoordinator.__init__`. I counted that keyword in core's `helpers/update_coordinator.py`: zero at 2024.10.0, one at 2024.11.0. It first appears there as `config_entry: config_entries.ConfigEntry | None | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED`.

So on 2024.8.x, 2024.9.x or 2024.10.x this raises `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'config_entry'` inside `async_setup_entry`, and the integration does not set up at all. Not a degraded mode, a total failure on the version you advertise as the minimum.

Everything else you use exists at 2024.8.0, which I checked individually rather than assuming: `async_schedule_reload`, `async_update_reload_and_abort`, the `version=` kwarg on `async_update_entry`, `async_at_started`, `SOURCE_IMPORT` and `DeviceInfo.serial_number`. So that one keyword is the only thing setting the bar. `"homeassistant": "2024.11.0"` in `hacs.json` and in both README lines.

Worth knowing that neither hassfest nor the HACS action checks the declared floor against the APIs actually used, which is why this went green.

## Smaller items

- There is no `custom_components/ubibot/brand/` directory anywhere in the tree. From Home Assistant 2026.3 that folder is how a custom integration ships an icon and logo, so on current versions this will render with no branding. Adding one, or opening a `home-assistant/brands` PR, fixes it.
- README line 21 says "only the ones your device actually provides will appear", and line 138 repeats it for the voltage sensor. `sensor.py` lines 51 to 53 create all six entities unconditionally for every channel; a field the device does not report yields an entity that exists and reads unavailable through lines 88 to 90. The behaviour is fine, the wording is not.
- README line 86 recommends 300 seconds but does not mention that the options flow clamps the interval to 60 through 3600 (`config_flow.py` lines 466 to 468).
- The illuminance unit moves from `lux` in the predecessor to `lx` here. `lx` is the correct Home Assistant value and `lux` never was, but migrating users with existing long-term statistics will see the unit-changed repair notice on that one entity. Worth a line in the FAQ so it does not arrive as a surprise.
- The `CHANGELOG.md` heading for 1.1.0 says 2026-07-19 while the tag was published 2026-07-26.

The rest is genuinely clean, and clean on the things most submissions in this queue get wrong: no blocking I/O, no dangerous builtins, no HTTP views, no credential in any of the ten log call sites, a sixteen-entry `TO_REDACT` applied to both entry data and every coordinator payload, `requirements: []`, no `async_timeout`, `ConfigEntryAuthFailed` raised properly with a real reauth flow behind it, no failure path returning cached data, `available` gating on `last_update_success` before its own two extra checks, no hardcoded entity IDs, no Lovelace writes, and an options flow that stores the entry under a private name so it works both below 2024.12.0 and above 2025.12.0. That last one is the check most submissions fail.

On the unique I

payload.body:
Hi @berkansezer77, thanks for merging master in back on the 6th. Here is the proper pass.

First, so it does not worry you: the red checks on this PR are not yours. Run `31117979409` failed at "Set up job" with `Failed to resolve action download info. Error: Service Unavailable`, so Hassfest and the JSON schema check never actually executed. Everything that did run passed, and your own repository's validation is green on the `v1.6.2` tag commit. That just needs a rerun on our side.

Reviewed against `v1.6.2`. The declared floor of `2024.11.0` is exactly right: `AlarmControlPanelState` and the `alarm_state` property are absent from core at 2024.10.0 and present at 2024.11.0, so you identified the binding constraint correctly. Three entities documented and three shipped, one service documented and one shipped with the field list and the `mode` options matching the schema exactly. And the auth posture is better than most: all five views are `requires_auth = True` *and* separately gated on `request["hass_user"].is_admin`, the panel is registered `require_admin=True`, and the free-form service step passes the caller's context so Home Assistant's own permission check still applies. The exponential lockout on wrong disarm codes, with a critical notification, is a nice touch.

Four things.

## The integration writes to and deletes from the Lovelace resource store

`__init__.py` lines 406 to 481. It reaches into `hass.data.get("lovelace")`, mutates `resources.loaded = True` after calling `async_load()` directly, then calls `async_create_item` at line 441, `async_update_item` at line 447, and `async_delete_item` at line 450, and retries the whole thing on a widening schedule out to two minutes.

Two problems with that, separate from the general point that an integration should not be editing the user's resource list.

Line 450 deletes every `sentinel-alarm-card-*.js` resource entry that is not the one it wants. That is a delete of an entry the integration did not necessarily create, made without asking.

And `async_unload_entry` at lines 511 to 513 removes none of it. Uninstall the integration and the resource stays, pointing at a URL that no longer serves anything.

You did get the YAML-mode guard right, and your comment explains why you avoided `add_extra_js_url`, which is a real consideration. The answer is to ship the card as a separate `plugin` submission, where HACS writes that resource as the package manager acting for the user and the user knows it happened.

## The stored disarm code is used to bypass its own check

`engine.py` line 1673:

```python
await ent.async_alarm_disarm(self.config.get("code") or None)
```

reached from auto-arrive (line 1759), the clock schedule (line 1702), entity triggers (lines 1732 and 1739) and the push notification Disarm button (line 1852).

Your own comments at `__init__.py` lines 188 to 190 and `alarm_control_panel.py` lines 335 to 338 explain exactly why passing the stored code would make code protection meaningless, and then this path does it. Anyone who can trigger one of those automations, or tap the Disarm action on a notification, disarms without knowing the code. For an alarm integration that is a design decision that at minimum needs to be in the README, and probably needs to be opt-in.

## `async_unload_entry` leaks on every reload

Same lines 511 to 513. It unloads platforms and returns. It never pops `hass.data[DOMAIN]`, never removes the `sentinel_alarm.arm` service, never calls `engine.stop_auto()`, and never unsubscribes the `mobile_app_notification_action` bus listener registered at `engine.py` line 1859.

That listener is added once per setup with no unsub stored, so every reload stacks another handler, and each one of them can disarm the alarm. On an alarm integration that is the one thing you do not want accumulating.

## A 25 MB blocking read on the event loop

`__init__.py` line 314, inside `async def post`:

```python
payload = field.file.read(MAX_UPLOAD + 1)
```

payload.body: Hi @dudeofawesome, thanks for stripping the reindent and rebasing; the diff is one line in the right slot now and it merges clean. Here is the review pass. Reviewed against `v1.0.0`. This is nice work: 64 IR command codes with a hand-written TOTO encoder and an XOR checksum, `docs/IR_CAPTURE_FINDINGS.md` documenting the live capture session it came from, and ten parametrised tests asserting real payload checksums. Entity accounting is exact, 19 buttons plus 5 switches plus 8 selects plus 1 event against the same 33 keys in `strings.json`, no orphans either way. Declaring `dependencies: ["infrared"]` with no `requirements` is exactly right and mirrors what core's own `lg_infrared` does. Two things. ## Blocker: the declared floor is two releases below the API you use `hacs.json` line 3 declares `"homeassistant": "2026.4.0"`, and README line 14 repeats it. The integration imports `InfraredEmitterConsumerEntity` (`button.py` line 8, `switch.py` line 7, `select.py` line 7), plus `InfraredReceiverConsumerEntity`, `InfraredReceivedSignal` and `async_get_receivers` (`config_flow.py` lines 8 to 12, `event.py` lines 9 to 12). I counted `InfraredEmitterConsumerEntity` in core's `homeassistant/components/infrared/__init__.py`: zero at 2026.4.0, zero at 2026.5.0, two at 2026.6.0. The component exists from 2026.4.0, but at that point its `__all__` is only `DOMAIN`, `InfraredEntity`, `InfraredEntityDescription`, `async_get_emitters` and `async_send_command`. The consumer-entity split into `entity.py` and `helpers.py` lands in 2026.6.0, and that is where all four of your names appear. Corroborating: `commands.py` line 12 imports `from infrared_protocols.commands import Command`. Core at 2026.4.0 pulls `infrared-protocols==1.1.0` and imports `Command` from the package root; the `commands` submodule path only resolves on the newer library that 2026.6.0 brings in. So on 2026.4.x or 2026.5.x, HACS installs this and the config flow dies with an `ImportError`. `"homeassistant": "2026.6.0"` in both places. ## Thirteen entities silently lose availability tracking `switch.py` line 103 and `select.py` line 281 override `async_added_to_hass` and never call `await super().async_added_to_hass()`. The switch override restores the last state and connects the dispatcher, then returns. `TotoWashletEntity` defines no `async_added_to_hass` of its own, so the override shadows `InfraredEmitterConsumerEntity.async_added_to_hass`, whose only job is `self._async_track_availability(self._infrared_emitter_entity_id)`. The 5 switches and 8 selects therefore never pick up the emitter's availability and never subscribe to its state changes: they report available even when the IR emitter behind them is gone. The 19 buttons and the event entity have no override and are correct. `RestoreEntity` is unaffected, since core restores through `async_internal_added_to_hass`, so adding the `super()` call costs you nothing. ## Smaller items - `__init__.py` lines 29 to 32 implement `async_reload_entry` as a hand-rolled unload then setup. `hass.config_entries.async_reload(entry.entry_id)` does the same thing through the framework's own bookkeeping. - `hacs.json` says "Toto Washlet" and `manifest.json` says "TOTO Washlet". Cosmetic, but they should agree. - `custom_components/toto_washlet/brand/icon.png` duplicates the root `brand/icon.png`, and Home Assistant only reads an in-tree `brand/` folder from 2026.3 onward, which your floor will now clear anyway. - `docs/IR_CAPTURE_FINDINGS.md` records only nozzle up and down while `commands.py` lines 90 to 94 ship five discrete `NOZZLE_POSITION` codes. Those are working notes rather than user documentation, so this is housekeeping. Bump the floor to 2026.6.0 in `hacs.json` and the README, add the two `super()` calls, and push a release. I will look again. ../Frenck

payload.body: Hi @AboveColin, thanks for the rebase. The conflict is cleared and the checks are green on the head, so here is the proper pass. Reviewed against `v1.0.0`, which is what the PR body links. The entity accounting is exact: 23 sensor descriptions shipped, 23 translation keys, 23 rows in the README table, no extras and no omissions in either direction. The `fitdays` package on PyPI is real and exact-pinned, and every one of the 62 symbols the integration touches exists in the wheel. Diagnostics emits field-presence booleans rather than measured values, which is a genuinely thoughtful choice for a body-composition integration. The coordinator raises `ConfigEntryAuthFailed` rather than `UpdateFailed` on an auth error and has a real reauth flow behind it, and `available` gates on `last_update_success`. Three things. ## `hacs.json` declares no version floor The whole file is: ```json { "name": "Fitdays", "content_in_root": false } ``` `config_flow.py` line 117 calls `self._get_reauth_entry()`. I counted occurrences in core's `config_entries.py`: zero at 2024.10.0, one at 2024.11.0. So the accurate floor is `"homeassistant": "2024.11.0"`. Without it, HACS offers this to any version, and on anything older the failure is the worst kind: setup works, everything looks fine, and then the first time the token expires the reauth step raises `AttributeError`. That is the path every user eventually walks. ## Two README statements that do not match the code README lines 92 to 94 say that on a weight-only weigh-in the body-composition sensors "hold their last known good value". They do not. `sensor.py` lines 34 to 37 is: ```python def _get(latest, _profile, _data): return getattr(latest, attr, None) if latest else None ``` and the upstream `is_weight_only` is `body_fat_pct is None and impedance is None`, so those attributes are absent and every one of those sensors goes to `unknown`. There is no last-good-value retention anywhere in the component. Either implement it or change the sentence; the `weight_only` attribute on the weight sensor already flags the situation correctly. README lines 85 and 86 say heart rate "stays unavailable otherwise". It goes to `unknown` rather than `unavailable`, since `available` depends only on the coordinator and the profile. The field name cited there, `measureHeart`, appears nowhere in the shipped code either; the related name is `measures_heart_rate`. ## The brand is not registered `home-assistant/brands` returns 404 for both `custom_integrations/fitdays/icon.png` and `logo.png`, and there is no open PR for it, so the integration will render with no icon in the UI. The four PNGs under `custom_components/fitdays/brand/` do not help with that; Home Assistant reads brand assets from that repository, not from inside the component, and only reads an in-tree `brand/` folder from 2026.3 onward. Worth knowing that `icon.png` and `logo.png` are byte identical to each other, as are the two `@2x` files. ## Smaller items - The stored `password_hash` is `MD5(MD5(password + salt))`, which is password-equivalent against this vendor's API and sits unencrypted in `.storage` like any config entry. Your README is accurate about this and does not overclaim, and the vendor protocol forces it, so I am noting it rather than asking for a change. - `.github/workflows/HACSAction.yml` and `.github/workflows/validate.yaml` run the identical action on the same triggers. - Dependabot PR #1 has been open since the day the repository was created. Add the floor, correct the two README sentences, and open the brands PR. I will take another look after that. ../Frenck

Fixed in [v1.0.1](https://github.com/AboveColin/HA-Fitdays/releases/tag/v1.0.1).

- `hacs.json` declares `"homeassistant": "2024.11.0"`. I checked the same way you did: `_get_reauth_entry` is absent from `config_entries.py` at 2024.10.0 and present at 2024.11.0.

That repository no longer accepts custom-integration icons: it closed my last such PR ([home-assistant/brands#10847](https://github.com/home-assistant/brands/pull/10847)) with "we no longer accept brand icons for custom integrations in this repository", citing the same announcement. Hi @somansch, thanks for the rebase back at the start of August. Here is the proper pass.

I reviewed against `v2.1.2`, which is the current release; the PR body still links `v2.0.0`, and the action run it points at predates two releases. The documentation is unusually precise: I counted every documented entity, attribute, event field, service field and config option against what ships and every one matched exactly, twelve attributes, ten event fields, eleven config fields, and the route-corridor sample-point arithmetic in the README even works out to the 21 points the code produces.

Three things.

## `hacs.json` declares no version floor

The whole file is four keys and none of them is `homeassistant`:

```json
{
  "name": "Lufop Radar",
  "render_readme": true,
  "zip_release": true,
  "filename": "lufop_radar.zip"
}
```

`config_flow.py` line 15 imports `section` from `homeassistant.data_entry_flow` at module level and uses it at lines 60 and 75. I counted `class section` in core's `data_entry_flow.py`: zero at 2024.6.0, one at 2024.7.0. So the accurate floor is `"homeassistant": "2024.7.0"`, and without it HACS offers this to versions where the config flow raises `ImportError` at module load with no actionable message.

The `zip_release` and `filename` pairing is right, incidentally: the release asset is named exactly `lufop_radar.zip` and the workflow builds it with the manifest at the archive root, which is what that flag needs.

## The radar markers keep showing stale positions through an outage

`LufopLocationEvent` at `geo_location.py` line 134 extends `GeolocationEvent` directly and holds the coordinator by hand at line 140. It is not a `CoordinatorEntity`, it defines no `available`, and nothing in the file consults `last_update_success`.

When a poll fails, the coordinator keeps its previous `self.data` and still notifies listeners, so `_sync_entities` runs against stale data and every radar marker goes on reporting its last known position with `available` still true. Meanwhile `LufopTotalSensor` is a `CoordinatorEntity` and does the right thing, so during an outage the count sensor goes unavailable while the markers stay on the map looking live. For a speed-camera integration people use while driving, that is the wrong way round.

The coordinator itself is correct and I checked it specifically: the `raise UpdateFailed` at `coordinator.py` line 116 is inside the only handler, nothing swallows it, and no failure path returns cached data. It is purely the entity's availability wiring.

## A revoked API key never asks for a new one

There is no `ConfigEntryAuthFailed` anywhere and no `async_step_reauth` in the config flow, whose steps are exactly `user`, `area`, `waypoint`, `route_corridor` and `route_options`. A rejected key comes back as HTTP 4xx, becomes `LufopAPIError`, and `coordinator.py` lines 115 and 116 turn that into `UpdateFailed`. So the coordinator retries forever and the user is never prompted. On first setup it surfaces as `ConfigEntryNotReady` and retries forever there too.

You do surface Lufop's own message text rather than a bare status code, which is better than most, so the vocabulary to distinguish the cases is already there.

## Smaller items

- `sensor.py` line 25 is `class LufopTotalSensor(CoordinatorEntity)`, added to the sensor platform but not a `SensorEntity`. It overrides `state` rather than implementing `native_value`, and line 52 puts `{"state_class": SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT}` into `extra_state_attributes` instead of setting `_attr_state_class`. Set that way the recorder's statistics machinery ignores it, so the entity asks for long-term statistics and does not get them.
- Unique IDs key on the user-chosen display name (`geo_location.py` line 145, `sensor.py` line 37) rather than `entry.entry_id`. The duplicate-name abort you added in v2.1.2 does close the collision, and I could not construct a live one, but it is a guard bolted onto the wrong ID scheme, and the entity-registry pur

Hi @AboveColin, thanks for the rebase. Here is the proper pass.

Reviewed against `v2.0.0`, which is what the PR body links and the only release. The `liberty-global-gateway` package is real, published and exact-pinned, and every translation key the code uses exists with none orphaned. Diagnostics has a thorough `TO_REDACT` and even regex-scrubs MAC addresses out of the event log, which is more care than most submissions take. The socket call in the config flow is correctly executor-wrapped, and there is a working reauth flow.

Four things.

## `hacs.json` declares no version floor

The file is three keys and none of them is `homeassistant`. `config_flow.py` lines 17 to 21 import `SsdpServiceInfo`, `ATTR_UPNP_SERIAL` and `ATTR_UPNP_UDN` from `homeassistant.helpers.service_info.ssdp`. That module 404s at core 2025.1.4 and first appears at 2025.2.0; I checked both tags. So the accurate floor is `"homeassistant": "2025.2.0"`, and without it HACS offers this to versions where the config flow cannot import.

While you are in that file, the `name` is 148 characters listing five model numbers. That string is what a user sees in the HACS list, and it will wrap or truncate badly. "Liberty Global Cable Gateway" would serve better, with the model list in the README where it already lives.

## A busy session leaves every entity showing stale data indefinitely

`__init__.py` lines 124 to 129:

```python
except GatewaySessionBusyError as err:
    if self.data is not None:
        _LOGGER.debug("Gateway session busy; keeping previous data: %s", err)
        return self.data
```

Returning normally from `_async_update_data` means `last_update_success` stays true, so `available` at `entity.py` line 360 stays true and `system_health` keeps reporting ok. If someone leaves the router web UI open, every one of the 55 entities serves values from an arbitrarily old poll for as long as that lasts, with nothing but a debug line to say so.

I understand the intent, and your README explains it: flapping 55 entities to unavailable on a transient contention is worse than holding. But this is unbounded. Bounding it, replaying for a couple of consecutive cycles and then raising `UpdateFailed`, keeps the good property and drops the misleading one.

The same shape sits at lines 79 to 88 for the hosts read, where the previous host list is reused while the rest of the payload is fresh, so device tracker presence silently lags the other entities. That one does correctly re-raise when there is no previous data.

## A lockout is treated as an authentication failure

`__init__.py` lines 122 and 123 group `GatewayLockoutError` with `GatewayAuthError` into `ConfigEntryAuthFailed`. That tears down the entry and raises a "reauthentication needed" repair asking for credentials.

But your own README says a lockout is a few-minute cooldown that clears by itself with the correct password. So the user is told their credentials are wrong when they are not, and re-entering the same correct password is the documented remedy for a problem that was going to resolve on its own. Your config flow already distinguishes the two, with a separate `lockout` error string. `UpdateFailed`, or a backoff, is the right response at the coordinator.

## Five unserialised sessions against a device you document as single-session

There is no `asyncio.Lock` or `Semaphore` anywhere in the tree. Login and logout pairs appear at `__init__.py` lines 67 and 137, `button.py` 52 and 57, `number.py` 62 and 67, `switch.py` 94 and 101, and `config_flow.py` 108 and 124.

Your README says the gateway allows exactly one authenticated session. So pressing reboot, moving the LED brightness slider or flipping a switch while a poll is in flight opens a second login on the same client, and its `finally: logout()` revokes the token the coordinator is holding. Entity commands and polls can break each other, and the failure surfaces as exactly the session-busy error the code above then swallows. A single lock around t

Thanks, all four are fixed in [v2.0.2](https://github.com/AboveColin/HA-Liberty-Global-Gateway/releases/tag/v2.0.2), along with the smaller items.

payload.body:
Hi @oifdsifh, thanks for merging master back in August; the conflict is cleared. Here is the proper pass.

I reviewed against `v0.0.8`, which is what the PR body links and is the current release. I also checked the release asset against the tag tree file by file and they are identical, so nothing is smuggled into the artifact.

## Blocker: the sensor platform does not parse on the Python Home Assistant runs

`custom_components/ha_smg_emh_casa/sensor.py` line 205:

```python
except InvalidOperation, TypeError, ValueError:
```

Unparenthesized multiple exception types is PEP 758, new in Python 3.14. Below that it is a `SyntaxError`, not a warning. I compiled the file to be sure: `SyntaxError: multiple exception types must be parenthesized`, line 205.

`__init__.py` line 78 forwards `Platform.SENSOR`, so Home Assistant imports this module on every setup. On anything older than Python 3.14 the import raises and the integration produces no entities at all, on an installation that otherwise looks like it configured fine.

The fix is one character pair:

```python
except (InvalidOperation, TypeError, ValueError):
```

CI does not catch it because `ci.yml` lines 27 and 49 pin `python-version: "3.14"` and `.ruff.toml` line 3 sets `target-version = "py314"`. The whole toolchain runs on the one version where the bug is invisible. Your tests at `tests/test_init.py` lines 41 and 48 do assert on sensor states, so they would have caught this if anything ran them on an older interpreter.

## Blocker: the declared floor is fourteen releases too low

`hacs.json` declares `"homeassistant": "2025.1.0"`. Home Assistant's `REQUIRED_PYTHON_VER` is `(3, 13, 2)` as late as 2026.2.0 and only becomes `(3, 14, 2)` at 2026.3.0; I checked the constant at both tags. So with the syntax above, the true floor is 2026.3.0, and every version from your declared minimum through 2026.2.x is a hard failure.

These two are one problem. Parenthesize the handler and the code runs everywhere again, at which point the honest floor is `2025.2.0`, set by the `homeassistant.helpers.service_info.zeroconf` import at `config_flow.py` line 31, which 404s at 2025.1.0. That import is behind `TYPE_CHECKING` so it is a floor signal rather than a second break, but it is still what the code needs.

## A changed gateway password leaves the user stranded

`coordinator.py` line 30 raises `ConfigEntryAuthFailed`, which is correct and is the right separation from the `UpdateFailed` on the line below. Home Assistant responds to that by starting a reauth flow.

There is no handler for it. `EMHCASAFlowHandler` defines only `async_step_zeroconf` and `async_step_user`; grepping the whole tree for `async_step_reauth` and `async_step_reconfigure` returns nothing. So the flow starts and has nowhere to go, and the only way back is to delete and re-add the entry.

## TLS verification is disabled unconditionally

`__init__.py` line 53 passes `verify_ssl=False`, and `config_flow.py` line 41 passes `verify=False`. Your comment gives the reason, that the gateway uses a self-signed local certificate, and that is a real constraint for LAN hardware.

Two things about it though. The digest credentials travel over a channel with no verification at all, and there is no opt-in: a user who has installed the gateway's certificate, or who wants to know this is happening, has no way to say so. A `verify_ssl` option defaulting to off, or pinning the certificate on first connect, would keep it working while making the trade-off visible.

## Smaller items

- `scan_interval` is a required field in the config flow at `config_flow.py` line 168, with a 1 to 3600 second range, and the README never mentions it. The entire options flow at lines 188 to 285 is undocumented too. README line 36 says only "Enter the gateway host, username, and password".
- `custom_components/ha_smg_emh_casa/brand/icon.png` sits at a path Home Assistant does not read below 2026.3, and `home-assistant/brands` has no entry for this integration.

The unique ID on the line above is correctly `f"{entry.entry_id}_{self._station_id}_{data_key}"`, so the registry is fine. The entity ID is built from the station alone.

Hi @m4rkireland, thanks for the rebase and for keeping it mergeable since. Merging this. A few notes for a future release, none of them blocking: - `config_flow.py` line 261 pre-fills the reconfigure form's API token field with the stored token, declared as a plain `str`. That round-trips the secret back into the browser and renders it in the clear. Core convention is to make the user re-enter it, and a `TextSelector` with `type: password` if you keep the prefill. - `hacs.json` declares `"homeassistant": "2026.7.0"`, and the newest core API in the tree is `OptionsFlowWithReload`, which I checked is absent at 2025.7.0 and present at 2025.8.0. So the real floor is 2025.8.0 and you are excluding everyone from 2025.8 through 2026.6 for no reason the code requires. Safe direction, so entirely your call, but worth knowing. - `diagnostics.py` line 14 emits `runtime_data.data` wholesale, which carries node hostnames, service names and container names. The config allowlist above it is well done and the token is structurally unreachable, so this is about infrastructure topology rather than credentials, but it is the part a user pastes into a public issue. - `brand/icon.png` and `icon@2x.png` sit inside the component directory. Home Assistant reads brand assets from the `home-assistant/brands` repository, and only reads an in-tree `brand/` folder from 2026.3 onward. The coordinator raises `ConfigEntryAuthFailed` on an auth failure and reserves `UpdateFailed` for everything else, with a real reauth flow behind it, and it returns nothing on the failure path, so a broken Portainer goes unavailable instead of quietly serving a stale snapshot. And your differentiation claim in the README checks out: core's `portainer` integration does per-container stats and only reads `swarm_id` to group stacks, so the node, service and task level really is territory it does not cover.
